turns:
Summarise this for a general audience in about 120 words, then list the limitations a careful reader should keep in mind.

Later school start times and adolescent sleep: a two-year observational comparison

Background. Adolescents commonly sleep less than recommended on school nights. One proposed remedy is to start the school day later. We compared sleep, attendance and self-reported mood in students at schools that did and did not change their start time.

Methods. Four secondary schools in one regional district moved their first lesson from 8:15 to 9:00 at the beginning of the school year; three neighbouring schools kept an 8:20 start. We surveyed students aged 13 to 16 at all seven schools in the term before the change and again 12 and 24 months later. Sleep duration was estimated from self-reported bedtime and wake time on school nights. A subsample of 212 students wore wrist activity monitors for one week at each time point. Attendance data came from school records. Mood was assessed with a short questionnaire. In total 2,904 students completed the first survey and 1,781 completed all three.

Results. At 12 months, students at late-start schools reported sleeping on average 34 minutes longer on school nights than before the change, while students at comparison schools reported 3 minutes less. Activity monitor data in the subsample showed a smaller gain of 21 minutes. Reported bedtimes moved later by about 10 minutes at late-start schools. At 24 months the self-reported gain was 27 minutes. Unexplained first-period absences fell by 18 percent at late-start schools and were unchanged at comparison schools. Mood scores improved slightly at late-start schools at 12 months, but the difference between groups was no longer distinguishable from chance at 24 months. We did not find a difference in end-of-year exam results.

Discussion. A 45 minute delay in start time was associated with a sustained increase in school-night sleep of roughly half an hour, most of which persisted for two years. Schools chose for themselves whether to change, and the late-start schools served somewhat more affluent areas. Students who left the study were more likely to have reported short sleep at baseline. Families at late-start schools reported some difficulty with morning transport and after-school activities ending later.

Here's the README for an internal tool. It's accurate but nobody can follow it. Rewrite it as a quickstart that gets a new engineer to a first successful run, and move everything else under 'Reference'.

logsift

logsift is a command line program for searching and aggregating structured logs. It was originally written in 2021 by the platform group to replace a collection of shell scripts and has since been extended several times. It reads newline-delimited JSON from files or standard input. Gzip-compressed files are detected by extension and handled transparently. The program is distributed as a single binary through the internal package repository, and can also be built from source with a recent Go toolchain using the usual build command in the repository root, though this is rarely necessary.

The general form of an invocation is the program name, then a subcommand, then options, then one or more paths. The subcommands are filter, count, top and tail. The filter subcommand prints matching records. Matching is controlled by the where option, which takes an expression in a small language; expressions compare fields to values using equals, not-equals, greater and less operators and a contains operator for substrings, and may be combined with and, or and parentheses. Field names may be nested using dots. The count subcommand prints the number of matching records, optionally grouped by one or more fields given with the by option. The top subcommand is like count with grouping but sorts the result and limits it to a number of rows given with the n option, ten by default. The tail subcommand follows a file as it grows, like the standard tool of the same name, and accepts the same where option.

Timestamps are expected in a field named ts in ISO 8601 form. The since and until options restrict by time and accept either absolute timestamps or relative durations such as 15m or 2h. If records use a different field for time, the time-field option changes it. Output is JSON by default; the format option accepts table and csv as alternatives. Colour is used when writing a table to a terminal and can be disabled.

Configuration may be placed in a file named .logsift.toml in the home directory, where default values for any option can be set, and where named aliases for frequently used where expressions can be defined and later referenced with an at sign.

Known limitations: records larger than one megabyte are skipped with a warning; the contains operator is case sensitive; and memory use for count with grouping grows with the number of distinct groups.

If a leak is found, the repair quote comes back to the committee. A proposal to install rainwater tanks on the shed roof was welcomed in principle. Two members will collect quotes. Nobody was sure whether council permission is needed for tanks over a certain size; Bronwyn will ask.

Waiting list. There are 17 people on the waiting list and 4 plots that appear abandoned. The rules say a plot holder gets a written reminder after two months of neglect and loses the plot one month after that. Reminders went out six weeks ago. Two holders have replied asking to keep their plots; two have not responded. It was agreed to reallocate the two unanswered plots at the end of the month and to split one of them into two half plots for new members who want to start small. One observer objected that her neighbour, one of the two who did reply, has not actually set foot in the garden since. No decision was taken on that.

Compost. The three-bay compost system is overflowing and attracting rats. A motion to spend up to 450 on two enclosed tumblers passed seven to two. The dissenters preferred repairing the existing bays with volunteer labour.

Open day. Set for the first Sunday of next month. A budget of 150 was approved for seedlings to give away and a sausage sizzle. Volunteers are needed for setup; a sign-up sheet will go on the shed door.

Other business. A request from the nearby primary school for a class plot was discussed warmly but there was no agreement on whether the school should pay a fee. Deferred to next meeting.

Meeting closed after about ninety minutes.
